DisclosedValue.description:
One value from a source pack, at a concrete RFC 6901 pointer.

``value`` is required and may be null: a disclosed null is a field the source pack
carries as null, which is not the same thing as a field the LDF does not disclose.
DisclosedValue.title: DisclosedValue

PlacedOnMarket.description:
The date the manufacturer says this version was placed on the market.

``basis`` is required and has exactly one value, so the date can never appear in an
LDF without the statement that it is declared and not verified.
PlacedOnMarket.title: PlacedOnMarket

PreviousLdf.description: The link to the LDF of the version before this one: the chain (WP3).
PreviousLdf.title: PreviousLdf

Redaction.description:
A value withheld from the LDF: where it was, why, and a commitment to it.

No value is carried. The commitment is :func:`certanix.verify_core.ldf_commitment`
over the source digest, the pointer, the path's salt and the canonical value.
Redaction.title: Redaction

RefusalRecord.description:
A capability-gate refusal, carried exactly as it exists (C.6).

``document_b64`` is the refusal record's own bytes, unchanged. ``canonical_sha256``,
``key_source`` and ``key_hint`` are what that record says about itself, copied
verbatim; the verifier checks they agree with the bytes. No decision or reason field
is added: the refusal speaks for itself.

statement.const: The capability gate refused this system under test, and the refusal record is carried here as it was signed. No measured claim is made for this product version by this record.
statement.title: Statement

RefusalRecord.title: RefusalRecord

SaltCustody.description: Who holds the secret the salts come from, stated in the signed bytes.

statement.const: A secret from which the salt of every redacted path in this file is derived exists, and the manufacturer holds it. Certanix does not hold it. The manufacturer can release the salt of one path at a time. If the manufacturer loses the secret, honest redaction can never be proved for this file.
statement.title: Statement

SaltCustody.title: SaltCustody

SourcePackRef.description:
A source evidence pack, named by the digest of the bytes it was signed over.

``key_source`` and ``key_hint`` are copied verbatim from the pack's ``signature``
block and its cosign bundle (``verificationMaterial.publicKey.hint``), or null when
the pack does not carry them. They are what the pack SAYS about its signer, not a
finding about which key signed it.
SourcePackRef.title: SourcePackRef

description: The Liability Defence File (artifact type `ldf`): a disclosure-ready, signed selection of evidence for one product version, built from signed evidence packs through a named disclosure profile. Values may be redacted: each is listed with its reason and replaced by a salted commitment. Capability-gate refusal records are carried exactly as signed, and each version names the previous version's LDF by digest. A STANDALONE signed root with its own `schema_version` line, not a field of an evidence pack, so the pack schema does not move when this one does. FROZEN: a correction is a new version. Structural validity only.

framing.default: A Liability Defence File: a disclosure-ready selection of signed Certanix evidence for one product version. It is signed by Certanix over this document as presented, and it binds to each source evidence pack by the sha256 of that pack's canonical signed bytes. A source pack's own signature covers that pack only, not this file. The placed-on-market date is declared by the manufacturer and is not verified by Certanix. Proving a redaction honest requires the original pack and the release of that path's salt by the manufacturer. This file is evidence. It is not advice on the law, not a certificate, and no outcome is implied by it.
framing.title: Framing

title: Certanix Liability Defence File, schema 1.0
